title: Half-minimum-area bound for cylinder covers
exact_target: If finitely many cylinders $B_i+R$ $u_i$ cover a convex body $K\subset R^{3}$, with unit axes $u_i$ and measurable perpendicular bases $B_i\subset u_i\perp $ of finite area, must $\Sigma _i$ $area(B_i)\geq \tfrac12 $ $min_{|u|=1}area(proj_{u\perp }K)$? Costs are counted with multiplicity and base convexity is not required.
